title: Legal entity finance attributes
requirement: Each legal entity (a kernel organisation unit of the kind legal entity) shall carry finance attributes: entity code, tax registrations, default currency, default chart of account, billing and shipping addresses, numbering initials, logo for documents.
rationale: Documents belong to a legal entity; numbering and templates depend on it.
acceptance_criteria: Given a legal entity without default chart of account, When a request is created for it, Then the user must choose a chart of account and is told why.|Given a duplicate entity code, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given numbering initials set, When a document is numbered with the dynamic prefix on, Then the initials appear in the number.

title: Finance masters per legal entity and organisation
requirement: Chart of accounts, account strings, budgets and fiscal calendars belong to a legal entity; an organisation under a legal entity uses that entity's chart of accounts and may have its own budget lines; coding a document to an account string of another legal entity is refused; budgets and consumption are reported per organisation and consolidated.
acceptance_criteria: Given organisation A under legal entity L1, When a request in A is coded, Then only L1 account strings are offered.|Given a string of L2, When used on A's document, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given budget lines per organisation, When the consolidated report runs, Then totals per organisation and the group total are shown.

title: Owning organisation on every record
requirement: Every master record (supplier, item, supplier item, catalogue, contract, category, tax code, payment term, ship-to location, template) and every document (request, order, shipment notice, receipt, return, invoice, credit note) shall carry an owning organisation and a sharing mode through the kernel pattern (TF-220); documents take the organisation of the requester or buyer and never mix organisations; the organisation is shown on lists and records.
rationale: Decision F-13: separation by business unit from day one.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user of organisation A creating a request, When saved, Then the request's organisation is A.|Given a request of organisation A, When a line references an item private to organisation B, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a list, When loaded, Then the organisation column is shown and filterable.
notes: Was FF-180. The owning organisation and the sharing mode are the kernel's (TF-220: S1, A1, A3; sharing modes in A8); this requirement keeps the business rules FF-180 adds.

title: Sharing modes for master data
requirement: Master data shall support the three sharing modes: global (default for categories, units, currencies, tax codes and payment terms), shared with listed organisations (for example a supplier or item used by two units), and private (visible to the owner only); administrators set the default mode per master type and may change a record's mode with audit.
rationale: Shared where it helps, separated where required.
acceptance_criteria: Given an item shared with organisations A and B, When a user of C searches, Then it is not shown.|Given a record changed from global to private, When saved, Then documents of other organisations that already reference it keep working and a warning lists them.|Given a change by a user without the master's configuration permission, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-181. The three sharing modes are the kernel's (TF-220, A8); this requirement keeps the default mode per master type and what a change of mode does to documents.

title: Organisation-specific configuration
requirement: Numbering sequences, document templates, approval configurations, tolerances, budget validation switches, receipt approval requirement and default match levels shall be settable per organisation, overriding tenant values for records owned by that organisation (TF-221); the tenant console shows effective values per organisation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a numbering sequence for organisation A with prefix A-PO, When an order of A is issued, Then its number starts with A-PO.|Given no override for B, When an order of B is issued, Then the tenant sequence is used.|Given a template missing for both A and the tenant, When rendering, Then it is refused naming the template. (error case)
notes: Was FF-183. The organisation scope of configuration is the kernel's (TF-221: settings in A6, numbering and templates in S4, approval configurations in S5); this requirement keeps which business configuration is set per organisation. Open point G-03 (section 12.2).

title: Items
requirement: Items (code auto or manual, name, description, type product or service, unit, category, commodity, tax classification, default price and currency, attributes, images, status) shall be maintained with translations for name and description.
rationale: Standard items for requests and catalogues.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new item with auto code, When saved, Then it receives the next code.|Given an inactive item, When a requester searches, Then it is not offered.|Given a duplicate manual code, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Categories and commodities
requirement: A category tree with management groups and a commodity hierarchy mapped to categories shall classify items, request lines, suppliers and contracts and shall be usable in approval conditions and reports.
acceptance_criteria: Given a category with a management group, When a request line of that category is submitted, Then the group can be resolved as approvers.|Given a duplicate category name under the same parent, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a commodity moved, When viewed, Then its items keep the mapping.

title: Units of measure
requirement: Units with code, name, type and conversions (for example 1 box = 12 each) shall be maintained; conversions apply when receipts or invoices use a different unit than the order line.
acceptance_criteria: Given an order in boxes and a receipt in each, When received, Then quantity is converted and compared in the order unit.|Given a unit without conversion to the order unit, When used on a receipt, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a duplicate unit code, When saved, Then it is refused.

title: Item imports
requirement: Items shall be importable through the kernel import framework with templates and validation.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid item file, When imported, Then items are created and codes allocated.|Given rows with unknown units, When imported, Then they are reported and skipped. (error case)|Given a dry run, When finished, Then nothing is created and the report shows counts.
notes: Was FF-049, the items; supplier items are CAT-006. Placed by the test: the import of the item master belongs with it.

title: Chart of accounts and segments
requirement: Finance administrators shall define charts of account per legal entity with ordered segments (name, length, data type, allowed values or value ranges, mandatory), buying group, billing address, and default match levels for products and services.
rationale: Account strings are built from segments.
acceptance_criteria: Given a chart with three segments, When an account string is entered, Then each part is validated against its segment values.|Given a chart of another legal entity, When selected on a document, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given segment values changed, When existing documents are viewed, Then their strings are unchanged.

title: Account strings
requirement: Valid account strings shall be stored as master records (string, segment values, owner, active) so that budgets, lists and reports reference them; invalid combinations shall be refused and inactive strings shall not be selectable on new lines.
acceptance_criteria: Given an inactive string, When a line is coded with it, Then it is refused with the status shown. (error case)|Given a new combination allowed by segment rules, When first used, Then it is created as a master record (if the setting allows) or refused (if the setting requires pre-defined strings).|Given a string owner, When a budget line owner is not set, Then the string owner is used as the dynamic approver.

title: Budget periods
requirement: Finance administrators shall create budget periods (name, start, end, owner, status Open or Closed) per legal entity; closed periods accept no new reservations.
acceptance_criteria: Given an Open period, When a line is split to it, Then it is accepted.|Given a Closed period, When a new request uses it, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given overlapping periods for one legal entity, When saved, Then a warning is shown (overlaps allowed for quarters inside years).

title: Budget lines
requirement: Budget lines shall be unique per budget period and account string, with owner, amount, reserved, consumed and available, and a consumption history with document references.
acceptance_criteria: Given a duplicate period and string, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given amount 100,000 with reserved 20,000 and consumed 30,000, When viewed, Then available shows 50,000.|Given history requested, When viewed, Then each row shows document type, number, amount and event (reserved, confirmed, released).

title: Budget availability check with reservation
requirement: When a request, non-order invoice or other budget-relevant document is submitted and budget validation is on for its type, the system shall lock the budget lines in a fixed order, compute required per split, compare with available, block or warn per configuration, and reserve the required amounts in the same transaction.
rationale: Gap: race conditions in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given two requests submitted at once against the last 1,000 available, When processed, Then one succeeds and the other is refused (blocking) or warned (warning mode).|Given no budget line for a string with validation on, When submitted, Then "No budget line exists for account string X" is shown. (error case)|Given warning mode, When exceeded, Then submission proceeds, the shortfall is stored on the document and shown to approvers.

title: Budget consumption and release
requirement: Reservations shall become consumption at approval (or at submission when configured), be released on rejection, cancellation or close-short, be transferred from request to order to invoice without double counting, and be reversed by credit notes.
rationale: Correct available budget at all times.
acceptance_criteria: Given an approved request later converted to an order and invoiced, When viewed, Then the budget line shows one consumption, not three.|Given a request cancelled, When processed, Then its reservation is released.|Given a credit note approved, When processed, Then consumption decreases by its amount. (edge)|Given a release attempted for a reservation that no longer exists, When processed, Then it is refused and reported as an integrity error. (error case)

title: Budget adjustments and transfers
requirement: Permitted users shall adjust a budget line (positive or negative, reason mandatory) or transfer between lines in one action, never below consumed plus reserved, with approval when configured.
acceptance_criteria: Given an adjustment that would make available negative, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a transfer of 10,000 from A to B, When approved, Then A decreases and B increases by 10,000 with one audit trail.|Given adjustments, When listed, Then actor, reason and time are shown.

title: Budget reports
requirement: Budget consumption by line, period and document type with reserved, consumed and available, and drill-down to documents.
acceptance_criteria: Given consumption, When the report runs, Then totals match budget lines.|Given drill-down, When clicked, Then documents are listed.|Given export, When run, Then a file is produced. (edge)|Given a user without the budget report permission, When run, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Fiscal calendar
requirement: Fiscal years with periods (no overlaps, no gaps) per legal entity, with open and closed states; documents carry the fiscal period of their date; closed periods refuse new documents dated inside them unless the user has the permission to post into closed periods.
acceptance_criteria: Given periods with a gap, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a document dated in a closed period, When created by a user without the permission, Then it is refused.|Given a document, When viewed, Then its fiscal period is shown.

title: Currencies and exchange rates with revisions
requirement: Currencies (code, decimals, symbol) and exchange rates (from, to, chart of account or legal entity, validity range, rate) shall be maintained through a revision workflow (draft, submitted, approved, applied), with a rate feed connector as a later option; conversions use the rate valid on the document date.
acceptance_criteria: Given a revision approved, When applied, Then rates are valid from the start date.|Given overlapping validity for the same pair and scope, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given no valid rate, When a line is converted, Then the save is refused with the pair and date named.

title: Tax codes and classifications
requirement: Tax codes with components and rates, validity and country, tax classifications for items and services (such as harmonised codes), and a place-of-supply rule setting shall drive tax lines on orders and invoices; totals round per currency decimals using half away from zero; country-specific rule sets (Indian GST with CGST, SGST and IGST by place of supply) are delivered as accelerator packs (BF-204).
rationale: Correct invoice totals; Indian GST readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Given a line of 1,000 with an 18 percent code of two components, When computed, Then two tax lines of 90 each are created.|Given an expired tax code, When used on a new line, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given rounding, When totals are computed, Then line taxes round to two decimals and the header equals the sum of lines.

title: Payment and shipping terms
requirement: Payment terms (net days, discount percent and days) and shipping terms shall be maintained and defaulted from supplier to order to invoice; invoice due dates and discount dates shall be computed from terms.
acceptance_criteria: Given terms net 30 and an invoice date, When saved, Then the due date is 30 days later.|Given a discount of 2 percent within 10 days, When viewed, Then the discount date and amount are shown.|Given a term deleted while in use, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Nightly reconciliation of budgets
requirement: A nightly job shall recompute budget reserved and consumed from the consumption history, whose rows name their documents (BF-064), compare them with the stored values, write differences to a drift report and alert operators; drift is an incident, not auto-healed. It runs in the one nightly reconciliation window of the kernel's jobs (TF-120 to TF-124).
rationale: Counters are a cache; documents are the truth.
acceptance_criteria: Given consistent data, When the job runs, Then zero drift rows exist and a success record is stored.|Given a manual database change that breaks a counter, When the job runs, Then the drift row names the line and values and an alert fires. (error case)|Given the job fails, When detected, Then an alert fires.
notes: Was FF-133, the budgets. Business recomputes from its own consumption history and needs nothing from the products (ADR-0042). Orders, Receiving and Invoicing reconcile their own counters in ORD-121, RCV-083 and INV-027, in the same window.

title: Ship-to locations
requirement: Ship-to locations per legal entity or unit with addresses shall be offered on lines and carried to orders.
acceptance_criteria: Given locations for the unit, When a line is edited, Then they are offered.|Given a location of another legal entity, When saved on the line, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a location on the line, When the order is created, Then the order line carries it.

title: Warehouses and locations
requirement: Warehouses and locations per legal entity (code, name, address, active) shall be maintained in a screen and offered on receipts.
rationale: Gap: no screen in the current product.
acceptance_criteria: Given a warehouse created, When a receipt is made, Then it is offered.|Given a duplicate code, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a warehouse deactivated, When used on a new receipt, Then it is not offered.

title: Location types and bill-to locations
requirement: Every location shall have a type, ship-to, bill-to or warehouse, and be linked to its legal entity; each legal entity has one default bill-to location, and more are allowed.
rationale: A legal entity is billed at an address of its own, sometimes at more than one, and the locations master already holds the ship-to locations and the warehouses.
acceptance_criteria: Given a legal entity with two bill-to locations, one of them its default, When a billing address is chosen for a document of that legal entity, Then the default is proposed and the other is offered.|Given a bill-to location without a legal entity, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a second bill-to location marked default for the same legal entity, When saved, Then the first loses the default.|Given a warehouse, When billing addresses are offered, Then it is not among them.
notes: Decided at the PRD split's checkpoint (section 12.1). The billing address among a legal entity's attributes (BF-001) is its default bill-to location.

title: Supplier master
requirement: The supplier master shall hold identity (number auto or manual, legal name, trade name, type, registration type, country), tax identifiers (validated per country rules), classification (categories, commodities, preferred flag, diversity attributes), commercial defaults (currency, payment terms, shipping terms, match levels), portal settings (allowed channels), status fields and custom fields.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier with unique identifiers, When saved, Then it is visible to buyers with status.|Given a tax identifier already registered, When saved, Then it is refused naming the field. (error case)|Given India validation on, When a GST or PAN with a wrong format is entered, Then it is refused.

title: Supplier addresses
requirement: Addresses (type, lines, city, state, country, postal code, one primary, one remit-to) maintained by supplier or buyer, used on orders and invoices.
acceptance_criteria: Given a second address marked primary, When saved, Then the first loses the primary flag.|Given an address used on an open order, When deleted, Then it is refused; it can be deactivated. (error case)|Given a remit-to address, When an invoice is created, Then it defaults to it.

title: Supplier contacts
requirement: Contacts (name, email unique, phone, role) shall be maintained; a contact with portal access is a Supplier Network user of the supplier organisation and is visible to the tenant as a linked contact; the tenant never holds supplier credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Given a network user of the supplier organisation, When the supplier is opened in the tenant, Then the user is listed as a linked contact with name, email, phone and role.|Given a buyer tries to set a password for a supplier contact, When saved, Then it is refused because the tenant never holds supplier credentials. (error case)
notes: Was FF-027, the contact data; the portal users are SPX-005. AC1 and AC2 are written for the split from the requirement's own clauses.

title: Supplier sites
requirement: Sites (name, address, tax registration, contacts, bank link, status) with site-level approval when configured; orders may target a site; invoices carry the site's tax registration.
acceptance_criteria: Given a site with a tax registration, When an invoice for that site is created, Then the registration is used.|Given a site without mandatory documents when required, When published, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a site deactivated, When a new order is created, Then it is not offered.

title: Supplier bank accounts
requirement: Bank accounts (bank, branch, account number encrypted, codes, currency, primary, attachments) shall be maintained; unverified accounts shall not be used for payment instructions.
rationale: Bank account change fraud is the main payables risk.
acceptance_criteria: Given a bank account saved, When the database is read without the application, Then the account number is unreadable.|Given a bank account whose verification is not complete, When it is chosen for a payment instruction, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-029, the account data and the rule that an unverified account is not used for payment; the verification is SUP-023. AC1 and AC2 are written for the split from the requirement's own clauses. Decision F-05 confirmed.

title: Supplier configuration defaults
requirement: Tenant administrators shall set defaults for new suppliers (payment terms, currency, match levels, required sections, required documents, portal channels) applied at creation and editable per supplier.
acceptance_criteria: Given defaults set, When a supplier is created, Then fields are pre-filled.|Given a default changed, When existing suppliers are viewed, Then their values are unchanged.|Given a user without the configuration permission, When saving, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Supplier categories and preferred status
requirement: Suppliers shall be classified by categories and commodities they serve, with preferred or approved status per category; request and order supplier suggestions shall use these classifications.
rationale: Guide buyers to the right suppliers.
acceptance_criteria: Given a line of category X, When suppliers are suggested, Then preferred suppliers for X appear first.|Given a supplier removed from a category, When suggested, Then it no longer appears for that category.|Given a supplier on hold, When suggested, Then it is excluded. (edge)|Given a category that does not exist, When assigned, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Supplier enablement per organisation
requirement: A supplier shall register once per tenant and be enabled per organisation with organisation-specific terms (payment and shipping terms, currency, match levels, preferred flag, status On or On Hold); documents of an organisation may use only suppliers enabled in it.
rationale: One registration for the supplier, separate control for each unit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a supplier enabled in A but not B, When a buyer of B creates an order for it, Then it is refused with an enablement action offered. (error case)|Given organisation terms set, When an order in that organisation is created, Then the organisation's terms default.
notes: Was FF-182, the enablement and its terms. Its optional organisation approval is SUP-006, since Business never depends on a product (ADR-0042); its clause that supplier users see the documents of every organisation that enabled them, with its AC3, is SPX-004's, which says the same. Decision G-01 default.

title: Document type settings
requirement: Settings per document type for budget validation and blocking, consumption trigger, multi-currency lines, approval configurations, numbering, templates, mandatory custom fields and acknowledgement reminder days.
acceptance_criteria: Given a setting changed, When the next document is created, Then it applies.|Given an invalid value, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a change, When audited, Then before and after are recorded.

title: Document templates for the products
requirement: Templates for order, change order, return note, receipt note and invoice acknowledgement per legal entity and language through kernel templates, with product placeholders documented.
acceptance_criteria: Given a template per legal entity, When rendered, Then it is used.|Given a missing placeholder, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)|Given a preview, When requested, Then sample data renders.

title: Approval configuration starter set
requirement: A starter set of approval configurations per document type (manager chain by amount bands, budget owner for requests, finance for invoices above a threshold, procurement head for suppliers) shall be seeded as inactive examples that administrators can activate and edit.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new tenant, When the console opens, Then the starter configurations exist inactive.|Given activation, When a document is submitted, Then the configuration applies.|Given an edit, When saved, Then it is versioned by the kernel workflow. (edge)|Given a starter configuration edited to reference an unknown field, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)

title: Go-live checklist and data readiness
requirement: A tenant readiness view shall show what is missing before go-live: legal entities, chart of accounts, account strings, budgets, currencies, units, taxes, templates, numbering, approval configurations, suppliers, items, users and roles, with links to fix each.
rationale: Goal 3 (first request within one day, section 1.2).
acceptance_criteria: Given missing templates, When the view loads, Then it is listed with a link.|Given all items complete, When the view loads, Then it shows ready.|Given a user without administration permission, When opening, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-175. Its checklist is made of contributions to the kernel's IUnitReadiness (A8). Its dependency on the supplier onboarding configuration (SUP-005) is dropped: Business never depends on a product, and a product that needs readiness items contributes its own to IUnitReadiness (TF-223, ADR-0042).

title: Organisation readiness checklist
requirement: Adding an organisation shall open a readiness checklist (legal entity link, chart of accounts, account strings, budgets, numbering, templates, approval configurations, enabled suppliers, users and roles).
acceptance_criteria: Given a new organisation, When created, Then the checklist lists missing items with links.|Given a user without administration permission, When they open an organisation's readiness checklist, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-188, the checklist's items, which this layer contributes to the kernel's IUnitReadiness; creating, deactivating and merging organisations are the kernel's TF-223 (A8). AC2 is written for the part, as BF-202 AC3 says it for the tenant.

title: Country accelerator packs
requirement: Country-specific rules shall be delivered as accelerator packs installed per tenant by operators and configured by tenant administrators: reference data (tax codes and components, classifications, document types), validation rules (identifier formats, e-invoice fields), computation rules (for example Indian GST: CGST and SGST for intra-state, IGST for inter-state by place of supply, reverse charge flags) and report formats; packs are versioned and upgradable without code changes to the products.
rationale: Decision F-08: Indian GST as an accelerator pack; other countries later.
acceptance_criteria: Given the Indian GST pack installed, When an intra-state invoice line is taxed, Then CGST and SGST components are computed; inter-state produces IGST.|Given no pack installed, When a line is taxed, Then plain tax codes apply without country rules.|Given a pack upgraded, When installed, Then existing documents keep their computed values and new documents use the new rules.|Given a pack installation by a tenant administrator without operator rights, When attempted, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-176. Its dependency on e-invoicing readiness is reversed: INV-010 applies the packs' e-invoice field rules and depends on this requirement (ADR-0042). Decision G-05 default: operators install, tenant administrators configure.

title: Reference data from standards
requirement: Categories shall support UNSPSC codes (with tenant-specific trees mapped to UNSPSC), items and locations shall support GS1 identifiers (GTIN, GLN), currencies ISO 4217, dates ISO 8601, locations UN/LOCODE and shipping terms Incoterms 2020, each as optional reference attributes that packs and integrations can rely on.
rationale: Common language with ERPs, suppliers and networks.
acceptance_criteria: Given a category mapped to a UNSPSC code, When exported, Then the code is included.|Given an item with a GTIN of wrong length or check digit, When saved, Then it is refused. (error case)
notes: Was FF-202, the reference data of the masters; the payment status codes (ISO 20022) with AC3 are INV-045, since Business never depends on a product (ADR-0042).

title: Masters import, export and ERP sync
requirement: All finance masters shall be importable and exportable through the kernel import framework and API, with ERP as the optional system of record (inbound sync by schedule) and conflict reporting when a record changed in both systems.
rationale: Every tenant loads masters from an ERP.
acceptance_criteria: Given a chart of accounts file, When imported, Then segments and strings are created and errors reported per row.|Given a record changed in both systems, When synced, Then it is reported as a conflict and not overwritten. (error case)|Given an export, When run, Then files per master are produced.

title: Use of master records by the products
requirement: Business shall declare an extension point through which each product answers which of its live documents use a given master record; a master record in use shall be refused deletion and may be deactivated instead, and a change of a master's sharing mode shall list the documents of other organisations that use it (BF-004).
rationale: Masters refuse deletion while documents use them (BF-072 AC3, BF-102 AC2) and list the documents a narrowed sharing mode affects (BF-004 AC2). The documents are the products', and Business never depends on a product (ADR-0042), so the products tell Business through a point it declares and they implement.
acceptance_criteria: Given a payment term used on an open order, When its deletion is requested, Then it is refused naming the order, and deactivation is offered. (error case)|Given an item shared with organisations A and B and used on a request of B, When its sharing mode becomes private to A, Then the warning lists that request.|Given a master record no product uses, When its deletion is requested, Then it is deleted.|Given a product that does not answer, When the deletion of a master is requested, Then it is refused naming the product, not allowed. (error case)
notes: Written at the checkpoint, after the design session's first answer: the one place where Business must hear from the products. Every product whose documents use masters implements it, and its Dependencies section says so (section 6.2).
